processes.description: A customer such as Great River Energy asks for a trader price on a fixed forward, hedge or firm gas volume at a named delivery point, or asks to close out an existing forward contract. The request often reaches a desk contact first and is forwarded to the person who can get a quote, sometimes with a request to call the customer that day. That person checks with the traders for bids or quotes, works out the close-out terms where a contract is being unwound, and gets back to the customer with the price.
steps: A customer asks for a price quote on a forward, hedge or firm gas volume, or asks to close out a forward contract.
The contact who receives the request forwards it to the person who handles customer pricing.
That person checks with the traders for current bids and quotes at the requested location and volume.
For a close-out, the remaining contract terms are valued against current prices.
The quote or close-out price goes back to the customer by phone or email.

stalls.summary: Requests reach a contact who does not price them and are forwarded on, with the new handler asked to call the customer the same day, so each round depends on finding the right pricing contact before any quote work starts.

automation.approach: A reusable quote-request message that captures customer, product type, delivery point, volume, term and response deadline and goes straight to the pricing desk, with current forward prices for that point pulled alongside so the trader confirms rather than looks up the quote. Close-out requests carry the contract reference so its remaining terms can be valued from the deal record.
automation.rationale: The visible friction is routing and missing details: requests get forwarded and the handler is asked to phone the customer. A reusable request message that collects every detail the trader needs and names the pricing contact helps most; the trader's judgement on the price stays manual.

work_estimate.rationale: Minutes go to checking with traders for bids at the requested point and volume, valuing a forward contract close-out where one is asked for, and phoning the customer with the result. The quotes show the request and its routing but not the pricing work itself, so the range is wide: a simple bid check is quick, a close-out valuation takes longer.

processes.description: Desk and settlement staff send out the EPE and EES models, the EPE reconciliation sheet, hourly data files and Western pre-scheduled firm price reports to settlements, external customer contacts and desk groups. A round is one send: the file for the prior trade date is prepared and mailed, and sometimes forwarded on by the desk. Around it, the desk keeps recipient lists correct, asking senders to add or remove names and distribution groups, correcting a mis-addressed recipient, and checking that the reconciliation sheet is completed and source data is loaded before the file goes out.
steps: The source data for the trade date is checked as loaded, such as Gas Daily prices.
The model, reconciliation sheet or price report is prepared for that date.
The reconciliation sheet is completed even when there are no variances.
The file is mailed to the distribution list of settlement, external and desk contacts.
Desk staff forward the file on to further contacts where needed.
Recipient changes are requested and the sender updates the distribution list.

stalls.summary: The EPE reconciliation sheet was not completed, prompting a follow-up on the new reconciliation model's location and status and an instruction to complete it going forward.
A report waits on source data: Gas Daily prices were not loaded yet, so the sender had to keep checking back before the send could go out.

Distribution lists drift: files went to the wrong Bill Williams, names had to be added and removed, and a new sender needed a list of who is in the real-time group before the distribution could be set up correctly.

contradictions.summary: Practice and expectation differ on the reconciliation sheet: it was being left undone, apparently when there were no variances, while the desk asks that it be completed even when there are none.

automation.approach: A scheduled job that builds the model or price report once its source data is loaded, attaches the reconciliation sheet and mails one maintained distribution group, with a check that holds the send and alerts the owner when data is missing or the reconciliation sheet is blank. Recipient changes go to the shared group instead of each sender's personal list.
automation.rationale: The repetitive part is preparing and mailing the same files to the same people; the visible failures are a skipped reconciliation sheet, data not yet loaded and stale recipient lists. A short send checklist covering data loaded, reconciliation done even with no variances, and distribution group current addresses all three right away, ahead of any scheduling tool.

work_estimate.rationale: Minutes go to checking the source data is loaded, preparing the model or price report for the date, completing the reconciliation sheet and, in some rounds, updating the recipient list. The quotes show these files are routine and repeated, so most rounds are short; the high end covers a round with variances to reconcile or a list to rebuild.

processes.description: Risk, settlements and desk staff move deals from one risk book to another. Early rounds flip single deals or a whole book's contents into the right regional or desk book, such as FT-US/CAND-ERMS, often by a stated deadline. After the bankruptcy filing, rounds move auto-terminating deals and terminated counterparties' deals into bankruptcy books from attached lists, followed by lists of stragglers. The receiver moves the deals in TAGG, zeroes them in Sitara, recalculates and officializes the book, and cross-references the result with other groups' lists.
steps: A requester identifies deals to move: single deals in the wrong book, a whole book's contents, or terminated counterparties' deals.
The deal list is compiled or forwarded, often as an attachment, naming the source and target book and a deadline.
The book owner moves each deal to the target book in the risk system, zeroing bankruptcy deals forward in Sitara.
The book is recalculated and officialized after the move.
The moved deals are cross-referenced against the requester's final list and other groups' calcs.
Stragglers found later are sent and moved in a follow-up round, and wrongly moved deals are moved back.

stalls.summary: Cross-checks wait on others: risk was still waiting on a final list to cross-reference with its calcs while settlements kept sending the deal lists behind terminated contracts.
Reconciling a book with another party's records needed help and the exact deal terms, and ended with the approach being redone a simpler way.
Bulk moves are rarely complete in one pass: one more deal, more deals and repeated batches of stragglers follow the first list.
Some moves are reversed: transactions already moved to the bankruptcy book had to be moved back to the live side.
Moves carry tight deadlines and repeated reminders, such as by the end of today, as soon as possible and right away.

contradictions.summary: Who leads the termination and bankruptcy-book work is named differently: one note says Darron and the writer will handle terminations from now on after Scott moved to another project, while a later note says Greg Couch will lead the estate risk effort.

Instructions on target books change mid-stream: deals are first moved from NG-Price to the bankruptcy book, then a later note changes the book used for terminated deals and renames NG-Price, and some deals moved into the bankruptcy book are sent back to the live side.

automation.approach: A standard deal-transfer request layout listing deal number, counterparty, current book, target book, effective date and reason, plus a risk-system query that pulls every deal for a terminated counterparty and flags those not yet in a bankruptcy book, so stragglers surface in one pass. After the move, a check compares the book's deals and totals with the request list before the book is officialized.
automation.rationale: Rounds repeat the same move with lists that arrive in pieces and in varying formats, and keep producing stragglers and reversals. One request template with fixed columns lets the book owner move and check deals line by line, and is the input a query or bulk-move script would read; deciding which deals belong in which book stays with risk staff.

work_estimate.rationale: Minutes go to compiling or checking the deal list against counterparties and contracts, moving each deal to the target book in TAGG and zeroing it in Sitara, recalculating and officializing the book, and cross-referencing against other groups' lists. Single-deal flips are short; bankruptcy rounds with attached lists of many deals and a reconciliation take far longer, hence the wide range.
